A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same GyroSwin research. The main text, equations, tables, figures, and Appendices A–H are readable and can be matched despite revisions and relocation.

before.justification: v1 reports original GKW simulation experiments, surrogate evaluations, scaling results, diagnostic analyses, and ablations in Sections 4–5 and the appendices.

after.justification: v3 retains original simulation and surrogate results and reports revised baseline measurements, expanded saturation-rule comparisons, and an additional qualitative sampling-sensitivity finding.

M1.justification: The proposed 5D Swin architecture, zonal-mode separation, latent 3D–5D mixing, integrators, and multitask outputs are retained. The expanded training recipe documents the existing scaling experiment, whose Figure 3 curves are unchanged; it does not establish a new GyroSwin procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions use GKW ion-temperature-gradient turbulence under the adiabatic-electron approximation, retaining the linear/nonlinear tasks and ID/OOD evaluations. Figure 5's parameter distribution is unchanged. Appendix C's expanded generation account and cyclone-base-case terminology do not establish additional dataset or task coverage.

E2.justification: The main comparator families remain unchanged, but Appendix D.1 revises PointNet's stated coordinate encoding from sinusoidal encoding to per-dimension embeddings. Appendix H/Table 5 adds GPR and MLP to the comparison against GyroSwinLinear at both training-set sizes; v1 compared that variant only with QL.

E3.justification: Reported baseline configurations are substantially revised: PointNet's hidden dimension changes from 256 to 320, and Transolver changes from 256 dimensions/four layers to 512 dimensions/eight blocks. Appendix C also revises the initial temperature-gradient range from [1,12] to [3,12]. These are reported setting changes, without establishing which experiments were rerun; the additional large-GyroSwin training recipe is principally new disclosure.

E4.justification: Appendix D.1 newly reports experimenting with larger coordinate batches and finding diminishing returns beyond 65,536 points. The existing saturation-rule analysis is expanded and its results revised. Table 4's component ablations and the appendix rollout and zonal-flow case studies are retained.

E5.justification: Appendix H newly states that GyroSwinLinear is trained for three seeds at both training-set sizes. v1 already reports plus/minus values but does not specify this run count. The disclosure does not establish an increase in runs, and no formal significance test is added.

E6.justification: Tables 2, 3, and 5 and Figure 4 contain revised results. Table 3 replaces PointNet's 27,000 ms timing with 19.7 ms under a revised configuration and changes its ID/OOD spectral correlations from 0.61/0.66 to 0.49/0.54, below QL's retained 0.51/0.58. Table 5 changes 241-simulation GyroSwinLinear RMSE from 38.03/31.19 to 42.85/23.40 and adds regressor results. These are revised reports, not established same-setting performance gains.

T1.justification: The gyrokinetic derivation in Appendix A, saturation-rule fitting mathematics in Appendix B, and attention-complexity arguments in Appendix H.1 are retained. Equation (8) clarifies averaged-flux notation without introducing a new mathematical result or derivation.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution bullets, and conclusion retain the claims of scalable 5D surrogacy, nonlinear-physics modeling, improved heat-flux prediction, approximately three orders of magnitude speedup, and scaling to one billion parameters. The introductory rewriting does not redefine these contributions.

C2.justification: Section 5 reverses the baseline-failure explanation: v1 attributes the errors to noisy predictions producing excessive flux, whereas v3 describes predictions decaying toward zero flux and producing RMSE around 120. Appendix H also expands the interpretation to tabular regressors and explains QL's data-scaling benefit. Its broad claim of outperforming GPR is not supported on the 241-simulation ID split. Section 6's limitations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: Appendices C–D add substantial reproducibility information: two-pass simulation generation and selection, bfloat16 precision, and the existing large-data experiment's 500 epochs, 16 H100 GPUs, staged loss activation, and training times up to 336 hours. PointNet's embedding, encoder, and pooling dimensions are documented in greater detail. The earlier 15 TB-to-2.2 TB preprocessing-storage statement is removed.

R1.justification: Section 3 adds Galletti et al. (2025) and credits that work with initially introducing the 5D attention and up/downsampling layers. Appendix C adds cyclone-base-case positioning using the already-cited Dimits work. The duplicated Dimits 2000a/2000b entries do not represent two different studies.

P1.justification: There are localized rewrites of the introduction, failure explanation, data-generation account, baseline descriptions, and Appendix H discussion. Training descriptions are organized more clearly, the broken FNO table reference is repaired, and funding acknowledgments expand. The overall section structure and most prose remain intact.

P2.justification: Figure 4's spectral curves and scale are revised, with smaller icon and notation edits elsewhere. Table 5 is reorganized into side-by-side columns for 48 and 241 simulations. Several appendix displays move, including placing Figures 6 and 7 together; the other existing figures are retained.

improvement.justification: The expanded data-generation account and large-model training recipe improve reproducibility, while Table 5 supplies more informative comparisons. These gains are limited by unreconciled interpretations: Section 5 still describes the old diagnostic rankings, and Appendix H claims superiority to GPR despite 241-simulation ID RMSE of 42.85 versus GPR's 36.95. The added transparency provides a limited net benefit, rather than evidence of broadly improved experimental validity.
